Commentary.Commentary: Trent Boult and Tim Southee shared four wickets apiece on a seaming surface that had enough life on it. The pitch was definitely helpful to the fast bowlers but not unplayable as was proved by the Shakib-Sarkar stand. The visitors will hope to make the new ball count tomorrow morning to put pressure on the Kiwis. It should be another engrossing day's play. Join us tomorrow at 0330 IST for all the updates. Unfortunately, due to lack of television feed, there won't be commentary for this game but we will provide update after stumps.

A fairly even day of Test match cricket. New Zealand started well after opting to bowl with early wickets but Bangladesh responded with a counter-attacking century partnership between Shakib and Sarkar. Both stroked fluent tons on a lively surface but couldn't kick on to press home the advantage. From a comfortable 165/2, they slipped to 179/5 before Nurul rallied with the tail to ensure that they reached a respectable score.

TEAM NEWS - New Zealand are unchanged from the previous game while Bangladesh have made four changes. Three of them were forced with Mushfiqur Rahim, Imrul Kayes and Mominul Haque all injured while Subashis Roy has been dropped. Two Test debutants in NURUL HASAN and NAZMUL HASAN while SOUMYA SARKAR and RUBEL HOSSAIN also make their way into the XI.

NEW ZEALAND WIN THE TOSS AND OPT TO BOWL. Not a surprise at all considering the grass on the surface and there should be help for the pacers especially on the first morning of the game. Batting may get easier as the match progresses although the bowlers should get some assistance throughout.

On the other hand, New Zealand will know that they cannot always win games after conceding nearly 600 in the first innings. Apart from that, they had a good game with the batsmen in good touch. The surface here at the Hagley Oval does seem more lively although even the Basin Reserve pitch did appear to be pacer friendly before start on day one. Nevertheless, it seems like batsmen from both sides will have to fight it out on this pitch. Hello and welcome to the second and final Test of the series to be held in Christchurch. Bangladesh will still be reeling from the shock defeat in Wellington. To make matters worse, they are missing three key players including skipper Rahim in this game which will see Tamim leading Bangladesh. The tourists will hope to take the positives from the first Test and hope to rectify the mistakes. They do have the talent but will have to translate it into performances if they are to have any chance of leveling the series.
